items.title: Introducing Vercel CI
items.summary: Coding agents are opening more pull requests than ever, and each one waits on CI before anyone can review or merge it. Most CI systems run the entire workflow on every push, even a one-line change. The more your agents push, the more time you spend waiting on CI.Today, we're announcing Vercel CI in Beta. It runs only the tasks affected by your code change, and spins up only the compute those checks need, the same way  scales with your traffic.Fluid computeAt Vercel, our CI now keeps up with our coding agents. Time from  to "CI passed" is  than it was before.git push2-6x fasterVercel CI uses Turborepo to understand your tasks and which ones depend on each other. It reads , so if you're already using Turborepo, there's no separate CI config to write.turbo.jsonIf you're not on Turborepo yet, add  and the  package. It works in single-package repos too.turbo.jsonturboThen tag the tasks you want Vercel CI to run. is all you need to get started. No workflow YAML to maintain, no drift between your CI config and , and Remote Cache is on by default."tags": ["ci"]turbo.jsonWhen you or your agent push code, Vercel CI determines which tasks need to run based on the change. Tasks whose inputs haven't changed come from cache. The remaining tasks each run on their own machine, powered by , Vercel's compute layer, and start as soon as their dependencies finish.HiveVercel CI gives each task the compute it needs and nothing more.To get started, follow the  or prompt your agent from your repo:documentationOnce set up, you or your agent can watch and inspect CI through the , , or . When something fails, go straight to the failing task, see what's blocked behind it, and open its logs, or search across recent runs to see whether a test has been flaky all week.Vercel dashboardVercel CLIVercel MCPVercel CI posts a check to your pull request on GitHub, so your existing branch protection rules can block merges on failure, the same way they do today.Vercel CI has already completed nearly 8 million tasks across our own repositories and the private beta, and we're just getting started. We're working to keep shrinking the time between writing code and running it in production.As we work toward general availability, we plan to add: on all plans.  and try it on your repository.Vercel CI is available in Beta todayRead the docsRead moreHow it worksRunning your CI on VercelClosing the loopAdvanced observabilityA  CLI command for distributed execution before pushing codevc ciMore granular test selection
